# Saved JSON editor and export UI

Baseline: [project kickoff charter](../../TavernForge_Project_Kickoff.html). Scope: [saved JSON editing and export](../planning/JSON_EDIT_EXPORT.md), under the [approved hybrid design](../DESIGN_DECISION.md). The application version is **0.4.0-internal**, code **4**. This document describes implementation; executed build and device evidence belongs in [current status](../STATUS.md).

## Editing

The saved-project inspector offers an explicit editor for supported source kinds. Named controls cover the six character text fields, additional V2/V3 text fields, V3 group-only greetings, book name/description, and content/name for up to 100 lore entries. Native World Info entry keys use escaped JSON pointers without rewriting the keys. Overlong paths are omitted from named controls and disclosed. Other values can be set/removed through an advanced exact-path JSON-value input. Full specialized lore settings, manual creation and artwork remain later work.

Controls are views over the preserved raw tree. Missing values remain missing; wrong-type values open in JSON mode; a missing group-greetings input suggests `[]` but writes nothing until Apply. Existing field input shows its previous value and whether the result is a string or a parsed JSON value. Whole-document replacement is not offered. The parser rejects duplicate keys, malformed values and resource-limit violations. A bounded patch batch is previewed against the stored base; format markers cannot change. The editor shows pending paths and validation before the user saves a new revision. Schema-invalid edits may save as drafts, while strict export remains blocked.

The ViewModel owns field input, pending patches and current preview through activity recreation. Large JSON is never stored in a `rememberSaveable` Bundle. Value input is limited to 1 Mi UTF-16 characters and paths to 4096; rejected additional input cannot become a silently truncated committed value. The original source stays separate from current bytes and library titles. Save uses the persisted expected revision. Conflicts retain the pending editor; discard/reopen is explicit. Replacing the selected project or clearing inspection is rejected while edits are pending, and navigation asks before discarding unsaved work. Unsaved process-death recovery is not implemented and the editor says so.

The editor is a separate Navigation 3 destination with native Material controls. Library/inspector supporting panes are enabled only at the Material expanded-width breakpoint (840 dp), using `currentWindowAdaptiveInfoV2` and `WindowSizeClass.isWidthAtLeastBreakpoint`; compact and medium windows use Navigation 3's single-destination fallback even when the window is tall. The editor has no supporting-pane metadata. The expanded-pane directive retains Material's geometry/hinge settings but disables automatic destination focus, which otherwise can target the library search field and open the keyboard. In pinned adaptive 1.3.0 the directive's `copy` does not expose this flag, so the full constructor is used. This addresses the source-backed cause of automatic search focus; cold launch, explicit search/editor focus and resize behavior require device checks after this change.

`MainActivity` retains `enableEdgeToEdge`, now declares `adjustResize`, and its existing `Scaffold(WindowInsets.safeDrawing)` handles keyboard/system-bar space without a second IME inset. Input and button visibility still need device verification at multiple sizes/text scales.

## Export

Export is available for a valid saved supported document after closing/saving/discarding the editor. Preparation reloads the saved revision and rejects stale local state, then uses strict engine export on a background dispatcher. It freezes owned bytes and an export request identity tied to project, revision and selection. A native confirmation shows format, revision, byte count and whether edited JSON formatting may differ. No format conversion or implicit save occurs.

CreateDocument supplies the destination URI. While a preview/picker/write is pending, selection and mutation actions are blocked. Cancellation writes nothing. A result after loss of the in-memory request is declined. The writer opens the selected URI in truncating write mode on IO, checks cancellation, writes bounded chunks, flushes and closes before success is reported. Exceptions from opening, writing, flushing or closing produce a failure message, and the UI explains that the provider may have left a partial file. It never deletes a provider URI as guessed cleanup and never modifies the import URI. Repeated destination callbacks during a write cannot start another write.

## Verification handoff

The UI owner added 22 tests: 15 ViewModel cases cover explicit edits, immutable originals, reopen/revision behavior, explicit V3 repair, wrong-type preservation, malformed/format-changing edits, stale-save conflicts, replacement guards, repeated saves, invalid-export gating, bounded inputs, array Set replacement (including null), picker cancellation, frozen/repeated export and write failure; four writer cases cover exact output, partial errors, missing streams and flush/close errors; three field/path cases cover native escaped keys, omitted overlong paths and safe filename suggestions. The previous app tests remain in place; their repository fake implements the added edit contract without claiming persistence coverage.

The UI owner ran `git diff --check` and parsed the app manifest/string XML successfully. **No Gradle or device tests were run by the UI owner** because the supervisor is the sole build owner. Pure writer tests do not establish actual provider behavior. The supervisor must run app tests/lint/build and check edit/save/reopen/export, cancellation, migration of the installed library, rotation, IME and the real document picker before marking those behaviors verified.
